title: Catalog confidence framework and GTM notes
body:
Executive summary:

This note proposes a complementary GTM framing for the model catalog centered on a lightweight, task-driven confidence taxonomy ("Confidence Tiers"), concrete verification signals that map to buyer requirements, and a set of pragmatic messaging hooks for engineering and procurement stakeholders. The goal is to make open models actionable for customers by surfacing what we can guarantee (latency, throughput, repeatability), what we measure (quality signals), and how customers choose a model for a given task with predictable economics.

Why this is different than existing approaches:
- Moves away from generic "verified" badges to a multidimensional confidence label that surfaces tradeoffs (quality vs cost vs latency) per task class.
- Emphasizes reproducible verification artifacts (small eval suites + workload fingerprints + unit-cost estimates) that customers can re-run or request for custom prompt sets.
- Provides direct rebuttals to the common enterprise objections (governance, explainability, cost volatility) with product feature tie-ins.

Target audiences and primary value props:
- Engineering/ML leads: pick models that minimize rework and integrate with existing inference contracts (latency SLO, KV cache compatibility). Value: reduced ops surprises, lower integration effort.
- Product/Feature owners: choose models by task-level quality and cost delta. Value: predictable UX and budget.
- Procurement/Security: certified signals for compliance and control (data isolation, KMS integration). Value: auditable selection criteria for contracts.

Confidence Tiers (proposal):
- Tier A (Application Ready): Full verification on our standard task suites for the target use-case plus end-to-end perf SLOs. Suitable for customer-facing workflows where correctness and latency are critical. Includes recommended quantization profile and cost-per-1k-tokens estimate.
- Tier B (Integrate & Validate): Passes baseline quality signals and performance checks on short-context runs; recommended for internal tools or early pilot projects. Includes suggested evaluation prompts and a small validation harness for customers.
- Tier C (Exploratory): Uncurated open model variant with high variability; recommended only for experiments and internal research. Provides raw benchmark artifacts but no guarantees on tail latency or behavior.

Verification Signals (what we publish per-profile):
- Task accuracy proxies: task-specific metric(s) (F1, exact match, BLEU, or human-labeled quality buckets) on our canonical mini-eval.
- Consistency score: measured variance of outputs across repeated seeded runs and prompt perturbations.
- Latency P95/P99 at defined batch sizes and sequence lengths.
- Cost estimate: inference cost per 1k tokens using our hosted baseline configuration, and delta bands for Dedicated/Private.
- Safety heuristics pass rate: percent of eval prompts flagged for policy-sensitive content.
- Input-length sensitivity: degradation curve as sequence length increases (helps routing/buffering decisions).

Concrete artifact set per model profile:
- One-page profile: human-readable summary with Confidence Tier, recommended tasks, key metrics, and quick adoption checklist.
- Mini-eval bundle: 50–200 labeled prompts for the canonical task(s) and instructions to re-run locally in Dedicated/Private.
- Perf matrix CSV: measured latency/costs across common sequence lengths and batch sizes.
- Diff notes: changes vs previous profile (semantic or perf regressions) and pinned kernel/quantization details.

Positioning language (short form):
- For engineers: "Pick models by the behavior you need, not by model name. Our Confidence Tiers and reproducible eval bundles show you the real tradeoffs so you can ship with predictable latency, cost, and quality."
- For product managers: "Choose a catalog profile that matches the customer experience you want — Application Ready profiles minimize runtime surprises, while Integrate & Validate lets you pilot fast with clear guardrails."
- For procurement/security: "Profiles include auditable verification artifacts and runtime controls so your compliance team can sign off without bespoke evaluation cycles."

Competitive notes (quick scan):
- Generic LLM API providers: emphasize simplicity and model breadth but typically publish only aggregate quality numbers. Opportunity: we differentiate by task-first profile + reproducible artifacts.
- Self-hosted runtime vendors: strong on cost and control but leave verification and task-level guidance to customers. Opportunity: bundle profile artifacts + launch playbooks to reduce buyer effort.
- Model marketplaces: often focus on models-as-assets; they surface benchmarks but lack routing/cost context. Opportunity: combine benchmark signals with cost/latency and routing fallback policies.

Common buyer objections and suggested rebuttals:
- "Open models are risky/unstable": show consistency score and Tier classification; recommend Tier A profiles with regression alerts and auto-fallback to a verified variant.
- "How do we compare models for our edge-case prompts?": offer to run the mini-eval bundle with the customer's prompt set as a paid verification run; include this as a standard uplift for Dedicated customers.
- "We need explainability and audit logs": call out Private deployment + KMS + per-request tracing in Console; attach profile diff notes and dataset provenance.

GTM hooks and assets needed:
- Product: UI additions for "Confidence Tier" badge, per-profile one-pager viewer, and a downloadable mini-eval bundle zip.
- Docs & SDKs: one-click script to run the mini-eval locally and a sample notebook demonstrating how to compute consistency score.
- Sales enablement: one-pager for engineering buyers, procurement checklist for enterprise sellers, and a short demo script showing model selection by task.
- Launch comms: email template for users with notes about what a profile means, a blog post describing the Confidence Tier methodology, and an internal FAQ for CS.

Measurement and success criteria (first 90 days):
- Adoption: percentage of new Hosted API projects that view or download a profile before first production request (target 40%).
- Pilot conversions: fraction of pilots that pick a Tier A/B profile and graduate to Dedicated (target lift +15% vs baseline).
- Reduction in "model surprise" incidents (post-release regressions tied to profile drift) measured via incident count and eval regression alerts (target -30%).

Next steps and owners:
- Define exact metric computation recipes and canonical mini-eval templates (Owner: Rina Gupta, due 2025-10-03).
- UX mock for profile one-pager and badge placement in Console (Owner: Ethan Park, due 2025-10-17).
- Sales enablement materials and pilot offer wording (Owner: Maya Thompson, due 2025-10-24).
- Pilot with 3 existing customers to test verification uplift and pricing (Owner: Liam O'Connell, due 2025-11-14).

Open questions for the group:
- How strict should Tier A guarantees be re: exact model binary vs model family? Do we allow minor patch updates without re-verification?
- Should the mini-eval bundles be public by default or gated to paying customers?
- How to price a custom verification run for Dedicated/Private customers so that it is attractive but compensates for compute cost?

Appendix (examples of short profile copy for UI):
- "Application Ready — Optimized for short-form customer responses. Verified on our support-resolution benchmark; P95 latency 140ms at batch 8. Recommended for live chat."
- "Integrate & Validate — Good baseline quality for internal workflows. Includes a validation harness you can run in minutes to confirm on your prompts."
- "Exploratory — High variance model; use for research and non-customer-facing experiments only."

Notes: This doc intentionally focuses on operationalizable messaging and deliverables rather than the full methodology math. For the rigorous statistical definitions and threshold calibration, see CONFLUENCE:MC-1024-model-index (linked).

-- Maya
